Register the per-source Harrier domain clusters through
`hero_data.assigned_clusters`. An out-of-tree run assigned all 292 sources
against the pinned model: 162,535 shards, 18.7 B documents. Paths recompute
from the frozen model plus three constants, so nothing records a path map and
repointing the model moves every assignment with it.

The assign stage reads its input through Arrow rather than row dicts. On an
18k-row shard, `to_pylist` plus the list-to-numpy conversion cost 7.3 s against
2.5 s of FAISS search, while the Arrow buffer read costs 0.1 s. Output is
unchanged: on a production shard the columnar path reproduces `id`,
`cluster_5000` and `cluster_40` exactly, with `dist_5000` within 1.5e-06 from
BLAS summation order.

`assign_source` takes the embedding facts rather than an `EmbeddingAttrData`,
because the luxical and Harrier pipelines each define their own class and
`common-crawl-focus-2026-22`'s embeddings are a repartition output (#8270) that
carries no such payload.

Against the earlier `held/harrier-zephyr-pipeline` label run, 698,876 shared
document ids across three sources agree exactly on `cluster_5000`, the 40-way
view and `dist_5000`. Every registered path resolves to a sealed artifact whose
shard count matches its embeddings.

result.body:
Register the hero quality data as two Datakit steps and make the store-ready
dataset a StepSpec output. `bucket.quality_step` reads three co-partitioned leaves
of a source (the normalized shard for row order, the fusion score leaf, and the
content-type leaf), applies the per-type calibration, and writes one shard per
basename with `source`, `id`, `content_type`, `raw_score`, `score` and
`quality_bucket` in the normalized row order. Its artifact is the `QualityScores`
the store already consumes, so `build_clustered_store` reads it unchanged.
`hero_data.quality` resolves that step's identity, and `run.py --stage bucket`
produces it for every registered source.

`score_fusion.fusion_score_step` is the producer of record for the raw scores,
and follows the data flow #9694 gave the reference quality step: one Zephyr task
per shard on GPU workers reads each document's first 512 stored `input_ids` from
the source's Nemotron tokenize leaf (`iter_tokenized_documents` regroups chunk
rows) in lockstep with the normalized shard's ids, and the Harrier embedding by
position. No tokenizer runs on the worker. The step depends on the tokenize step
(`hero_data.tokenize_step_for(source, NEMOTRON_TOKENIZER)`), refuses a tokenize
artifact built from another normalize output or tokenizer repository before it
lists anything, and carries the tokenizer commit in its identity twice: through
the tokenize dependency's hash and through the pin. The Nemotron tokenize leaves
the August 14 run read were deleted from S3 after it, so the run's scores are
registered by path map as `hero_data.fusion_scores` rather than rescored; a
rerun of the score stage tokenizes the source again (the runner builds the
dependency) and lands at the step's own identity. The content-type leaves
written beside those scores are registered the same way as
`hero_data.content_type`, and `hero_data.harrier` now returns a frozen step so the
score step can depend on it.

Every input leaf of a source holds the normalized shard's documents in its row
order. A census over all 162,535 shards of the 292 sources found every
fusion-score, content-type and Harrier shard in exactly the normalized order, with
the same ids and row counts. Both steps therefore read their side inputs by
position and check each batch's ids against the normalized shard
(`AlignedColumn` for whole-column sides, `AlignedDocuments` for the streamed
tokenize side), so a leaf from a different normalize run fails its shard.
`QualityScores.samples_output_dir` is removed; the stage report reads its
spot-check text from the normalized shard of the same basename, and the reference
quality step from #9694 keeps its lockstep tokenize/normalize read without the
samples side output.

The model directory moves to `datakit/models/quality/nemotron_88k`, relative to
`MARIN_PREFIX`, with the config fields of the removed bigram, MoE, frozen-donor
and dtype arms dropped from `model.py` and the saved meta. `load_pooled_scorer`
resolves the artifact stem from the directory, so the token-window `PooledScorer`
from #9694 loads both `pooled_junkgate2_marin` and `nemotron_88k`. `QualityPin`
carries separate digests for the scorer artifacts and the calibration file,
checked by the worker before it writes, so a refit calibration moves the bucketed
dataset without moving or rescoring the raw scores. The calibration file parses
into a `Calibration` dataclass (global or per-type curves); `calibrate_model`
from #9694 writes it. Manifest entries for `harrier`, `fusion_scores`,
`content_type` and `quality` cover all 292 sources. The fusion checkpoint's
document-embedding weights form one optional `DocFusion` submodule whose field
order matches the serialized leaves, so the deployed checkpoint loads to identical
weights and scores.

The bucket stage has run over all 292 sources: 18,710,478,349 documents in
162,535 shards, equal to the fusion-score totals, in 2h50m with 12 sources in
flight on CPU workers. On `nsf_awards` (3 shards, 381,789 documents) the output
reproduced the normalized row order, the pinned raw scores and content types, and
the calibrated buckets on every row. The score stage was rerun on `nsf_awards`
from the tokenize leaf (Iris job `/muchanem/hero-quality-score-smoke-nsf`:
tokenize under Nemotron, then score against the pinned Harrier embeddings) and
matched the pinned scores row for row, same ids and order, to a maximum
difference of 1.56e-3 (mean 2.28e-4), the bf16 reduction-order noise of a
4,096-document batch against the earlier 32,768. A local end-to-end test runs
`score_fusion` over hand-written tokenize and embedding leaves with a tiny fusion
model and checks order, window truncation, chunk regrouping and the refusals.

result.body:
* fixes https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/8121
* the classifier that closed #6849 still sorts by domain — it ranks within math at Spearman `+0.086` and within code at `+0.328` against prose's `+0.621`, and puts 57% of documents in one bucket. the rubric was right; the label set behind it carried 530 math and 1,177 code labels
* relabel with GLM-5.2 across all 292 sources (87,948 labels, code `10,947`, math `5,179`), retrain, and calibrate per content type

within-type ranking on the training holdout, v0 → v3:

| type | v0 | v3 |
|---|---|---|
| math | +0.086 | +0.384 |
| structured | +0.441 | +0.696 |
| code | +0.328 | +0.532 |
| agentic | +0.263 | +0.472 |
| multilingual | +0.324 | +0.486 |
| prose | +0.621 | +0.691 |
| overall vs oracle | +0.454 | +0.641 |

* per-source signal preserved at `+0.728` — the model did not buy cross-type fairness by going blind to real source differences (source oracle means span `2.13` to `4.72`)
* bucket spread on the 50M sample: `10.6/15.7/39.9/24.4/9.3` against v0's `2.0/10.9/56.7/29.1/1.4`. top-two share `33.8%` vs `30.5%`
* `calibrate.py` fits one remap per content type — the types do not share a ceiling (solved agent traces reach the top score 3.4% of the time against prose's 26%). equal-count bands within a group were measured and rejected: per-domain mean quality runs `2.13`–`4.38`, so forcing equal mass ranks a quality-3.0 document above a 4.0 [^1]
* `content_type.py` predicts the type the calibration needs, since production sees only text. hashed tokens + structural features, held-out `0.834` — the accuracy is not the gate, the parity cost is, and that is `1.89x` with predicted types against `1.89x` with oracle types
* `gate_labels.py` blocks training on a poisoned label set, comparing against the *input* set because selective loss is invisible from the survivors
* `gate_model.py` compares a candidate to the deployed model on within-type ranking, parity and per-source signal

two labelling bugs, each of which produced a healthy-looking set:
* documents hard-cut at a character cap read as damaged, so the grader scored them 1 — Spearman(length, quality) `-0.25`, 85% of the bottom bucket at the cap. the labelling-layer analogue of #6859
* prompts over the context were rejected with a 400 and counted as ordinary drops, silently losing exactly the longest documents

one calibration bug, found by reading documents rather than by any metric:
* math carries 5,179 labels and `20` at level 1; that median placed its bottom cutpoint at `0.596`, above the 10th percentile of math's own scores, and sent `50.3%` of math to the bottom bucket including worked geometry. a cutpoint now requires labels on both adjacent levels and borrows the global one otherwise. every model-level aggregate preferred the broken version

acceptance:
* read test — 24 disagreements against v0, both directions, stratified by source: v3 defensible on `15` (62.5%). it kills SEO spam, job postings and product marketing that v0 rated mid-bucket, and fixes the non-English penalty. **residual: worked math and programming exercises still land about two buckets low**, consistent with math being the weakest type
* intruder test — first run void (336 abstentions of ~864 calls); the harness now attributes abstentions per side and retries a failed process instead of spending a trial. rerun gave 0 abstentions and an inconclusive verdict, and a confound was then found: v0 holds 63.5% of each domain in one bucket with a 10th/90th cell-size ratio of `0.009`, so its trials pit a large bucket against a handful of outliers. `--adjacent-only` confines trials to neighbouring buckets; that run is in flight

not resolved:
* **operating point** — v3 selects `33.8%` into the top two buckets against v0's `30.5%`. needs an explicit decision before this replaces the deployed model
* `gate_model.py`'s absolute within-type floor of `0.65` is mis-derived (training-set numbers applied to holdout measurements; the single-rater label ceiling on this classifier is near `0.62`). the relative comparison needs no threshold
* the intruder panel is one model in several seats, so it measures self-consistency, not agreement between independent judges

[^1]: `test_calibrate.py` asserts both halves — a compressed type recovers, a genuinely poor type does not — so calibration cannot be quietly swapped for rank-based bucketing.

Add launch_datakit_swarm_cw.py, which trains one grug-MoE run per candidate
mixture on the CoreWeave H100 fleet -- the successor to
experiments/mixing/v0/launch_swarm.py on the current executor framework. build()
returns one ArtifactStep per mixture and --max-concurrent bounds parallelism; the
model, optimizer, regime, and resources are shared across runs, so only the
168-bucket two-phase weights vary. Mixtures come from a JSON file (SWARM_MIXTURES)
-- the mixture-surrogate sample.py export or a plain list -- whose bucket names
match the datakit mixture space one to one.

Retarget launch_datakit_moe_mix.py from a us-central2 v4-8 TPU to CoreWeave H100
(the datakit store already lives on the CW object store under
s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/datakit/store_8ac06c74), refactor the two-phase data
config to take explicit per-mixture weights, and add DATAKIT_* env knobs for model
size, sequence length, batch, tracker, checkpoint location, eval, and simulated
epoching.

_bucket_path returned a store-relative path that levanter's TreeCache opened as a
local file and 404ed; it now resolves against MARIN_PREFIX. The heuristic
d512/256-expert config OOMs on one 8xH100 node at batch 512 x seq 8192 (a 32 GiB
fully-replicated FSDP activation tile), so DATAKIT_SEQ_LEN/DATAKIT_BATCH size a run
to fit -- seq 2048 matches the shape launch_cw_scale runs. CW S3 tensorstore
checkpoints abort mid-write, so the swarm writes node-local disposable checkpoints
and the single launcher takes DATAKIT_CHECKPOINTS=local.

A single-mixture run and a two-mixture swarm both reached the correct untrained
loss (~11.78) reading the real 168-bucket store from CoreWeave.

result.body:
Fit a shared-content transfer Gaussian process across registered data-mixture swarms and select two-phase mixtures for a target swarm. Historical swarms train the shared response; only observed target-swarm runs define the acquisition baseline.

The prior mean learns phase-specific penalties on squared simulated epochs. A phase-linked Matérn covariance shares content response across swarms and retains a same-swarm residual. Compiled JAX implements MAP fitting, exact posterior prediction, posterior-mean selection, and Monte Carlo noisy expected improvement without Ax, BoTorch, GPyTorch, or Torch.

Candidate mixtures satisfy the two phase simplexes on the 1/49,152 lattice. The campaign loader reads a commit-pinned public Parquet registry on Hugging Face, verifies artifact hashes, and persists the candidate pool, acquisition values, selected mixture, diagnostics, and provenance. The targeted package suite passes 30 tests on CPU.

result.body:
Add a `ruler` eval (lm-eval's 13-task RULER long-context group) and a capped
`ruler-smoke` to the experiments/evaluation launcher, grouped in a `longcontext`
suite. RULER carries a new `EvalTaskConfig.metadata` (its `max_seq_lengths`
ladder). The eval client routes a metadata-carrying task through lm-eval's own
CLI (`python -m lm_eval`) instead of the evalchemy fork's `eval.eval`, because
only lm-eval's CLI merges `--metadata` and `--model_args` into its TaskManager;
the fork builds the pretrain TaskManager without metadata and drops both, so
RULER's data-prep would crash without a tokenizer. The client clamps
`max_seq_lengths` to the served window (lm-eval left-truncates a longer prompt,
which would silently cut the haystack and score garbage), and `completion_only`
pins the raw-continuation completions route for base and chat models alike.

RULER stays out of `smoke`/`core`: it needs the evalchemy-tpu image rebuilt with
lm-eval's `[ruler]` deps (`wonderwords`, `scipy`; `nltk` is already baked), now
added to docker/evalchemy-tpu/Dockerfile. Until that rebuild and digest re-pin in
`marin.evaluation.evalchemy.runtime`, a RULER launch's eval child fails on the
missing deps.

Reimplements the stale WIP #6110, which was built on the since-removed
`lm_evaluation_harness_evaluator`. The eval now runs against the served endpoint
through the current launcher, taking its context window from the served
`max_model_len` and `--metadata` rather than vLLM engine_kwargs.

Add pinned OpenAI MRCR tasks to endpoint-backed Evalchemy with canonical nonce-gated SequenceMatcher scoring. Results include overall accuracy, nonce-prefix hit rate, and each supported context-length and needle-count cell. Preprocessing uses the deployed tokenizer and served context window to exclude requests that cannot fit.

Pass the checked-in task definitions into Evalchemy's isolated runtime. Full and one-example-per-cell smoke configurations use completion-style `User:` and `Assistant:` prompts for base checkpoints. Smoke selection stops after every potentially supported cell has one exact fitting example, avoiding repeated scans of the full 2,400-example corpus.

Add a parameterized Grug exporter for the step-141000, step-156000, and two step-157000 arms from #8701. It applies pending QB router bias, adapts the array-stacked training state to the inference model, casts weights to BF16, and records the serving-time context and qk settings. All four exports completed in `us-central2`; each contains 44 objects, 39 safetensor shards, and 134,175,089,683 bytes. Their configs advertise 262,144 tokens and qk multipliers 1.57, 1.57, 1.57, and 1.75.

Add `fsutil verified-copy` for the GCS-to-R2 move. The command uses fixed-size R2 multipart uploads, hashes source bytes during upload, verifies destination bytes, binds retries to the source object generation, and publishes a completion manifest last. All four R2 copies completed. Each destination contains 44 payload objects totaling 134,175,089,683 bytes and a schema-v1 completion manifest with 44 matching SHA-256 records. The step-141000 transfer resumed five verified objects after one scheduler preemption; all four jobs exited successfully.

Register the four R2 exports for H100 serving. Object-store metadata reads use the bucket router, evaluation jobs forward namespaced R2 credentials, and the native vLLM subprocess maps those credentials to its S3 client without replacing the parent process's CoreWeave storage configuration.

All four checkpoints completed generative MRCR on the same deterministic 299-example selection with 299/299 examples scored and no evaluation errors. Accuracy was 0.01221, 0.01310, 0.01254, and 0.01403 for step-141000/qk1.57, step-156000/qk1.57, step-157000/qk1.57, and step-157000/qk1.75. Prefix-hit rates were 0.12709, 0.14381, 0.15050, and 0.15050. The 262K 8-needle cells scored zero for every checkpoint; the other 262K cells were at or below 0.00176. Full records are linked from #8702.

A CoreWeave smoke against the Snowball 67B export completed all 12 cells through the 65K bin with zero Iris failures or preemptions. It recorded MRCR accuracy `0.004714223641098665` and nonce-prefix hit rate `0.16666666666666666`; the durable result and exported checkpoint paths are recorded in #8702.

result.body:
Let the hero switch context length mid-run without changing its training schedule. The ladder launcher takes `--seq-len` and holds 4,194,304 tokens per rack per update, so the sequence batch shrinks as the context grows (2816 sequences at 16K on 11 racks). The step count (390251), learning rates, decay, gate/router weight decay, and `run_progress` therefore match the 4K run. A changed context requires an explicit `--qk-mult`, applied to all attention layers; `--capacity-factor` overrides the expert receiver capacity.

Harrier now shuffles blocks of 2^20 tokens (`io_block_size = 2**20 // seq_len`), which equals the existing 256-sequence block at 4K. At a longer context the outer block permutation stays the same, so only each cell's in-progress 512-block window reorders. With the previous sequence-sized blocks, a 16K relaunch would have re-read an estimated 2.85T already-seen tokens of the remaining ~9T. At 16K the past main-mixture boundary moves from step 108000 to 108096, and a continuation must pass `--accept-mixture-boundary-shift`.

Canonical hero eval stays at 4K packing, so the inherited `eval_dropless/*` series remains comparable, and the first-step eval now also runs after a checkpoint resume. Per-example FLOPs rise with context, so a FLOPs baseline (`--flops-baseline-step`, `--flops-baseline-total`) keeps `throughput/total_gflops` continuous across the handoff. `trigger_hero.sh` records the context, QK multiplier, capacity, eval context, FLOPs baseline, and boundary acceptance in the W&B lineage and the #8506 launch record. `launch_diagnostics` gains `--optimizer-tokens-per-step`, `--gate-router-weight-decay`, `--eval-seq-len`, and `--eval-prefix`, so a one-rack rehearsal can use the hero's optimizer settings and report long-context eval separately.

The live run is unchanged. A switch still needs a GPU rehearsal from the handoff checkpoint and agreed trial thresholds; see the inventory and validation plan in #9615.

result.body:
# tl;dr

Checks that a saved HF export really holds the trained weights, and that frozen weights are unchanged. Comparing with the starting model only works when nothing trained, so this compares with the trained float32 weights instead.

## Detail

Verify an HF export against the actual trained FP32 masters, including per-tensor save casts, while requiring explicitly frozen tensors to retain their pinned source values. Comparing a trained export with the initial model alone would reject legitimate updates and miss an export of stale weights.

`levanter.compat.hf_export_audit` provides bounded safetensors index/header validation, a source-hash receipt, and the collective trained-export comparison. The caller supplies the complete `TensorSpec` mapping, frozen key set, metadata hashes and files, and optional config validator. There are no fixed Snowball tensor counts or archived experiment imports. Only the export writer reads saved payloads; ranks replicate one master tensor at a time using the existing writer-failure synchronization. Metadata checks retain the precise allowance for a tokenizer-config template matching the separately compared template bytes.

This extracts the reusable portions of the run-used `identity_context_distill/save_audit.py` and `precision_source_audit.py`. Those files are byte-identical at the original #10707 source and Path B run commit `69ddc88fb2ff4a6e45ee5cbbec866d9f86c2d068`. Model-specific 502-tensor/26-router policies remain in experiment callers on logbooks. The historical [offline export audit](https://gist.github.com/karansag/2ac0c5798b18bfdbec9a81b7090361d2#file-r7-offline-export-audit-reading-chukar-md) supplies context; the library does not treat that result as a generic runtime admission.

Restacked onto current main `e09e38188706` on 2026-11-04, based directly on #10705. Touched tests: 11 passed; lint, Pyrefly and advisory review passed. GitHub CI is tracked separately on the new head.

## How it was found

We first wrote the export audit for the zero-learning-rate probe. In that probe the export must equal the source checkpoint byte for byte. Probe r7 failed the audit only on metadata, because the tokenizer saver adds a `chat_template` field. All 502 tensors were equal. Once training made real updates, a comparison with the source no longer worked: it rejects real updates, and it cannot tell whether an export holds stale weights. So the audit now compares the export with the trained float32 masters, and it requires the frozen tensors to keep their source values. In the first 16-update run it found what we expected: 476 trained tensors changed and the 26 frozen router biases unchanged.

Part of #10695

Stack guide: the [Snowball identity PR stack guide](https://claude.ai/artifact/8Y2f2JyjQEnFnLZe5Qs5vn) covers the review order, why each layer exists, and where it acts in the forward pass.

Eval corpus preparation now stops before it seals a manifest when a required eval fails to load. The required evals are the lm-eval tasks gsm8k, humaneval, mmlu, mmlu_pro and leaderboard_mmlu_pro (every leaf task of each), the nine AA Intelligence Index benchmarks, and a new Uncheatable Eval suite: the seven subsets that `experiments/datasets/uncheatable.py` evaluates, pinned to upstream commit 185c4638 with exact record counts. The eval Bloom build takes a tuple of `RequiredEvalSuite`s and refuses to start unless the AA and Uncheatable manifests are complete and the lm-eval manifest lists every required leaf task.

The aa-index-v4.1.1-v3 corpus treated the lm-eval tasks as best effort. GSM8K failed in every region because the Hub no longer resolves the un-namespaced `gsm8k` ID, and MMLU failed on CoreWeave after a dropped connection. Preparation logged and skipped both, so the Hero's decontam marks (`_combined_fixed_8c17764d` Bloom, built from the CoreWeave corpus) never checked MMLU or GSM8K. Uncheatable Eval was never in the corpus, although the Hero evaluates it in its training loop.

The loader patch maps `gsm8k` to `openai/gsm8k`. Required lm-eval task loads and source downloads retry five times with exponential backoff, so a dropped connection no longer stops preparation. A sealed corpus version is immutable, so `EVAL_CORPUS_VERSION` moves to aa-index-v4.1.1-v5. The v5 corpus is staged and sealed in `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin`, `gs://marin-us-west4`, `gs://marin-eu-west4` and `gs://marin-us-central2`, the four prefixes that held v4, so the Datakit canaries can build the Bloom after merge. Each regional lm-eval manifest includes 811 leaf tasks, among them gsm8k, humaneval, all 57 MMLU subjects, leaderboard_mmlu_pro and the 14 mmlu_pro subjects; 116 other best-effort leaf tasks still fail.

The decontam viewer groups Uncheatable records (`uncheatable-<subset>-<record>`) by subset and reads their text from `uncheatable/<subset>/`.

The required suites and task names enter the Bloom step hash, which rekeys the reference pipeline and testbed Blooms. The Hero's pinned decontam paths do not change.

result.body:
Adds `experiments/sft_launcher`: a general-purpose chat-SFT launcher that expresses a full SFT run as a parameterized `sft_step(spec) -> ArtifactStep[LevanterCheckpoint]`.

The flow is native dataset transform (ShareGPT/OpenAI → canonical messages) → chat tokenize/pack with a **pluggable** chat template + completions-only masking → Levanter SFT (`initialize_from_hf` + `use_hf_model_config`) → HF export. The chat template, dataset mixture, model/init, sequence length, packing, and cluster target are all fields of `SFTSpec`, so nothing is hardcoded to a model family. It fills two gaps in the high-level helpers on current `main`: `marin.experiment.data.tokenized` cannot emit a chat format, and `marin.experiment.train.train_lm` inits from a checkpoint handle rather than `initialize_from_hf`.

`configs/delphi_1e22.py` is the first worked example (Delphi v0 chat template + magpie/warmup mixture); `delphi_chat_template.py` carries that template. `smoke_sft_tpu.py` is a preemptible-TPU end-to-end smoke of the generic `sft_step`.

Two device/vocab fixes carried here:

- **GPU-only `cuda_async` PJRT allocator.** The resume-OOM defrag fix (#7115) is set only when the target device is a `GpuConfig`. On TPU, passing `allocator:...` to `PJRT_Client_Create` aborts the backend and JAX falls back to CPU ("No accelerator found"), so it must be GPU-only.
- **`pad_tokenizer_to_match_model`.** Qwen (and others) pad the embedding vocab past the tokenizer's for TPU efficiency (Qwen3: model 151936 vs tokenizer 151669); without this the Vocab axis is built from `len(tokenizer)` while the checkpoint embedding is larger → a Vocab-axis pytree mismatch at `train_step` trace. No-op when they already match (e.g. the Delphi prepared tokenizer).

**Smoke validation (v6e-4, `--region us-east5`, via `iris --cluster=marin job run`).** The GPU-only `cuda_async` fix is confirmed: the run now clears JAX/TPU distributed init on the v6e-4 slice — the exact point where the earlier "Smoke A" aborted (`Unexpected option name passed to PJRT_Client_Create: allocator` → CPU fallback → "No accelerator found") — and proceeds through the dataset build, chat tokenize/pack, `initialize_from_hf` of Qwen3-0.6B, tokenizer-vocab padding, and into `train_step` tracing + fused-cross-entropy kernel selection.

Full train-steps + HF export on the tiny Qwen3-0.6B smoke are **not yet green**: after the vocab padding, a residual mismatch surfaces at `optimizer.update` — a `haliax.nn.mup.EmbeddingStandardParam` still carrying the unpadded `Vocab=151669` inside the optimizer state while the model/params are `151936` (Qwen3-0.6B has tied embeddings). This is a Levanter-internal interaction (padding not propagated to the mup param wrapper / opt-state for tied embeddings), independent of the `cuda_async` fix and of this launcher's ArtifactStep/dispatch logic, and it does **not** affect the real Delphi path (a prepared, vocab-matched tokenizer → padding is a no-op). Tracked as a follow-up.

The downstream evalchemy-on-TPU eval launcher is a separate PR.

Aligns the Grug 67B-A2B two-stage chat SFT with the `experiments/sft` construction on main. Model and data are now independent inputs to one shared `sft_step(spec, resources)` on marin's ArtifactStep flow, instead of a bespoke Grug launcher:

- **`ModelSource`** (a Protocol) owns the architecture, tokenizer, where the initial weights come from, and which backend trains it. `HfModel` inits from an HF checkpoint (`initialize_from_hf`); `LevanterCheckpointModel` inits from a native Levanter checkpoint or a chained upstream step; **`GrugModel`** plugs the native ring-EP `run_grug` backend and its weights-only init into the same step. Grug stays in the vendored `june_tpu_67b_a2b` tree because its `Transformer` pytree must match the cooldown checkpoint exactly and is not a Levanter-registry `LmHeadModel`.
- **`SFTSpec`** carries the data and hyperparameters; the chat template is a parameter (Delphi v0 is one instance). An experiment composes a model and a dataset mixture without touching the pipeline — the two Grug stages just swap `_JOB{1,2}_DATASET` and chain Stage 1's checkpoint step into Stage 2's `init_from`. Order is load-bearing: Stage 1 (`wildchat` plain chat) establishes the chat format from the step-42150 base; Stage 2 (Llama-Nemotron science-reasoning canonical-think) chains from it to build the reasoning region. Each stage is one packed epoch, sequence packing on, completions-masked (assistant span only).
- Training length is `num_train_steps` (explicit / mixtures) or `num_train_epochs` (single dataset), which resolves the packed-step count from the chat cache's token total at run time (#7244) — no hand-calibrated counts.
- `experiments/sft/configs/delphi_1e22.py` migrates onto this seam; the generated Delphi `TrainLmConfig` is byte-identical to before.
- Fixes a latent OOM in the shared conversation transform: its Zephyr workers were floored to 1 GiB (a `ZephyrContext` default) and got OOM-killed (exit 137) on wildchat's long conversations — raised to 8 GiB.

**Grug backend geometry (unchanged from the original launcher).** N=8 H100x8 / 64 GPU, expert-parallel=8 (256 routed experts over intra-node NVLink), `model_axis=1`, `replica=1`, bs=64, seq_len=32768, per_device=1. Tensor/model parallelism is architecturally impossible for this model: `model_axis>1` must divide both `num_kv_heads=5` (prime) and `vocab_size=128256`, and `128256 % 5 != 0`, so no valid width >1 exists — the run is pure data-parallel (bs=8N). Optimizer is AdamH not Muon (`GrugMoeAdamHConfig`): Muon's Newton-Schulz workspace is a ~21 GiB replicated per-device floor that never shards (`num_layers=26` is coprime to any expert-inclusive `batch_shards`) and OOMs at every node count (mirrors #6693). `ce_implementation="batched_xla"` avoids materializing the `[tokens, vocab]` logits tile (~15.7 GiB/dev at seq32k); attention is `gpu_fa4_cute` (the short `sliding_window=2048`). HBM fit ~68 GiB/dev under the 80 GiB ceiling.

Validated end-to-end on cw-us-east-02a at that geometry (8 nodes / 64 GPU): native step-42150 load → chat cache → weights-only init (step resets to 0) → 8 steps at loss 0.712 → checkpoint saved, no OOM.

Resolved Job 1 launch config (GrugMoeAdamHConfig, `ce_implementation=batched_xla`, `attention_implementation=gpu_fa4_cute`, N=8 / 64 GPU, data-parallel / expert=8, bs=64, seq_len=32768, AdamH fp32): https://gist.github.com/penfever/5896ce2ff7953a715ea5af76364cabc0

result.body:
The Delphi SFT config required its model_ref/tokenizer_path to point at a manually prepared checkpoint. The raw laion/delphi-* tokenizers leave the think/tool tokens as unnamed `<|reserved_special_token_N|>` slots, so `<|start_think|>` fragments into ~6 byte pieces and training on it is wrong. Preparing the checkpoint — renaming those reserved slots to single-id strings and reinitializing the corresponding embedding rows — was an out-of-band prerequisite with no reproducible recipe.

`prepare_checkpoint_step` provides that recipe as an `ArtifactStep`. Because the edit only touches the `embed_tokens` and `lm_head` rows (both live in one safetensors shard), it streams the base checkpoint from the Hub straight to the output prefix: the shard holding those tensors is rewritten in memory (reseeding the reserved rows with a truncated normal matched to the column mean/std, mirroring levanter `reinitialize_some_tokens`), and every other file is copied through byte-for-byte. Nothing else changes, so the untouched weights stay identical to the base and peak footprint is one shard rather than the whole model on disk. The renamed tokenizer replaces only the files `save_pretrained` regenerates; the base's `special_tokens_map.json` (bos/eos, rename-invariant) is copied through. `delphi_prepared_checkpoint_step()` is the concrete Delphi recipe for staging.

`SFTSpec.model` is a `ModelSource` — `HFModel` (a model_ref/tokenizer used verbatim) or `PreparedModel` (built by a preparation step and resolved as a dependency). `delphi_1e22` keeps the existing direct-`model_ref` approach via `HFModel`; the preparation step and `PreparedModel` path are there for future configs that want to build their inputs from a clean prefix.

The reserved-slot map alone identifies the edit, so the step is not tied to one model family.

Fixes #7243

result.body:
Run each evaluation as a StepSpec with its own lock, success cache, and result record. Evaluations in one launch share a candidate server and optional hosted judge. Cached evaluations are skipped on restart; a fully cached launch starts no servers. A group StepSpec locks the launch before starting inference so duplicate orchestrators cannot provision duplicate servers.

Evaluators run sequentially by default. `--max-concurrent` allows concurrent evaluators on shared inference, but omits per-evaluation server metrics because server-wide counters include sibling traffic. Server startup failures write infrastructure-failure records for all pending evaluations.

Pipeline retries derive run IDs from the pipeline artifact path and resolved model, evaluator, runtime, judge, and policy settings, preserving completed evaluations across orchestrator resubmissions. CLI launches and mutable pipeline versions (`dev` or `*-dev`) create fresh runs. Verified policies retain their pinned benchmark sources and Harbor/Evalchemy commits.

EvalDash withholds scores until each evaluation's StepSpec succeeds. Historical records without step status keep their existing display. A crash after writing a record but before StepRunner marks success can rerun that evaluation. The success cache prevents completed steps from being overwritten on ordinary restarts, addressing the failure in the [October 6 incident](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/627).

result.body:
This PR corrects four rules that give training the wrong reward or advantage on main.

Unfinished Nemotron Ultra replies score 0. On main, a reply cut off at the generation length limit, or with neither a final answer nor a tool call, is graded on its partial text: a length-stopped multiple-choice `\boxed{C}` and an empty reply to a forbidden-word instruction each score 1.0. The GenRM, Lean refinement and prompt-injection agents keep their own rules for such replies, and the abstention agent grades an empty answer. The multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) smoke recipes grade replies this way; they log the reward and train on teacher advantages. Tasks graded by taskcompendium graders do not use this rule.

Group baselines use only eligible final outcomes. GRPO, RLOO and RLOO-N compute each group's baseline from the final row of each trajectory whose `exclude_from_baseline` flag is false. On main, GRPO ignores the flag: in a two-row group with final rewards `[1, 0]` and the second row excluded, main gives advantages approximately `[0.707106, -0.707106]` while this branch gives `[0, 0]`. Excluded rows get advantage 0. Every row of a group gets advantage 0 when the group has fewer than two eligible rows (RLOO-N: fewer than its configured minimum) or when their rewards span at most 1e-6. Training with these estimators requires `generator.n_samples_per_prompt` of at least 2. In step-wise training, each row receives its trajectory's final-row advantage through its own response mask.

Harbor retries a failed trial only when its error treatment is mask, within the configured include and exclude lists and retry budget. On main, failures scored as zero are also retried: with classification enabled, `NonZeroAgentExitCodeError` gets a 1-second retry delay on main and no retry on this branch. With error classification disabled, every failure is treated as mask. The MOPD 32K recipe treats `ModelServerError` and `VerifierTimeoutError` as mask.

GSM8K grading defaults to `reward_method: final_line`: a reply earns reward only when it completed and its last line is `#### <number>` with the correct number. The iceball_micro, curriculum RL and on-policy distillation nightly GSM8K runs use this default.

Startup rejects `generator.weight_sync_pause.mode: abort` together with a vLLM tool parser, auto tool choice or reasoning parser. The launcher rejects `generator.apply_overlong_filtering`, `trainer.algorithm.enable_token_reward_channel` and `trainer.algorithm.rloo_n_filter_zero_reward_groups`; the training driver rejects `advantage_estimator: rloo_n_pbs` and the Harbor keys `enable_pbs_shaping`, `pbs_gamma`, `pbs_max_total_shaping`, `pbs_potential_shape` and `enable_token_reward_channel` at startup.

`think_token_weight` other than 1 requires Harbor `enable_span_tagging: true`; startup rejects it otherwise.

The Marin SkyRL CPU nightly, which trains CatCount with GRPO, passes on this branch: [run40391710835](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/actions/runs/40391710835). The effect on larger GRPO runs is not measured. PR CI does not collect `test_trainer.py`, `utils/test_policy_optimization.py`, `test_group_admission.py`, `rollouts/test_buffer.py`, `test_harbor_retry_config.py` and `inf_engines/vllm/test_openai_kwargs.py` under `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/tests/cpu/`; run them from `vendor/skyrl` with `uv run --isolated --frozen --extra cpu --no-group dev --with pytest==8.4.2 --with pytest-asyncio==1.4.0 pytest -q -p no:xdist skyrl-train/tests/cpu/<file>`.

result.body:
Add a one-off Datakit store builder that performs the existing attribute join and filtering while routing surviving documents directly into `(domain, quality, length)` caches. Documents with at most 64K tokens land in `lte_64k`; longer documents land in `gt_64k`. The canonical Datakit store builder and reference pipeline remain unchanged.

The successful Iris run produced `gs://marin-us-central2/datakit/store/june-67b-a2b-length64k/2026.08.24` from 114 source components. The final artifact has 200 short cells and 191 long cells. Short cells contain 11,722,087,779 documents and 8,554,200,622,073 tokens; long cells contain 6,470,523 documents and 1,818,143,081,980 tokens. The combined 11,728,558,302 documents and 10,372,343,704,053 tokens match the source store, including exact document and token conservation in every domain-by-quality cell.

Define `LONG_CONTEXT_SKEW` as a relative multiplier on the long-to-short sampling ratio within each domain-by-quality cell. The default of 1.0 reconstructs the original token-proportional mixture. Increasing the value renormalizes short and long weights inside each cell, so the second-phase domain-by-quality mass stays constant. For this store, long-context mass is 14.94% at skew 1 and 22.59% at skew 2.

A separate cooldown launcher consumes the length-partitioned components and skewed weights.
